# Platform Logging Checklist: U2 Log Events

**Purpose**: Test whether the requirements for moving the bot's log lines to Lambda's JSON log format are complete, clear and consistent. That covers the line keys U4 and U5 rely on, the alarm filters that must keep working, the staging check before production, and local behaviour.
**Created**: 2026-11-09
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), checked against [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md), [contracts/log-line.md](../contracts/log-line.md) and [quickstart.md](../quickstart.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Audience and depth**: the reviewer, before `/speckit-tasks` and again at pull-request review. Standard depth.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Does the spec state the full set of logging settings the function must have? FR-001 names the format and the application level, while the plan also sets the system level explicitly. [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. FR-001 says the system level keeps its default, while the plan and research set `system_log_level = "INFO"` explicitly and assert all three values. Fix: FR-001 names both levels as INFO, set explicitly, and the log group unchanged.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: FR-001 names the format, both levels (INFO, explicit) and the unchanged log group.
- [x] CHK002 Is it a stated requirement, not only an acceptance scenario, that an offline check pins the log format? US2 scenario 1 implies one, and the plan's `terraform test` assertion has no FR behind it. [Gap, Spec §US2]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. No FR requires the offline pin; only US2 scenario 1 and the constitution check imply it. Fix: FR-001 requires a `terraform test` assertion on the three settings.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: FR-001 requires an offline `terraform test` assertion on all three settings; US2 scenario 1 matches it.
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec define which keys of the runtime's line U4 and U5 may rely on, and say that the runtime's stack-trace keys are not part of the contract? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for what the bot's logging set-up does locally (CLI, tests), as opposed to "in the deployed function"? FR-002 is scoped to the deployed function only. [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK005 Does the spec say where the request id for the per-run history record comes from, now that the bot no longer stamps it on log lines? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "stack-trace behaviour" in FR-006 defined now that the runtime, not the bot, writes the stack trace? Does it mean only whether a call logs a trace, or also the key and shape it appears under? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. On `main` the trace is under `exception`; under the runtime it moves to other keys, so a literal reading of SC-003 fails. Fix: FR-006 defines stack-trace behaviour as whether a call records a trace; the key and shape belong to the runtime.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: FR-006 defines stack-trace behaviour as whether a call records a trace; key and shape belong to the runtime. SC-003 refers to it.
- [x] CHK007 Is "the first staging run after deploy" defined for a paused staging schedule, or for a run that posts nothing? SC-006 covers the second case; the spec says nothing on the first. [Clarity, Spec §SC-006, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK008 Is it clear which settings own the root log level: the function's application log level (FR-001) or the bot's own set-up (FR-002)? Both set INFO, and the spec does not say which wins if they ever differ. [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-002]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. `configure_logging()` sets root INFO on every invocation and overrides the runtime's level; nothing says which wins or that they must match. Fix: FR-002 says the two must stay equal, or drop the root `setLevel`.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: FR-002 says the code's root level is the one in effect and must equal the application level; research R2 records why both are kept.
- [x] CHK009 Is "the same decisions, captions and output as on `main`" (SC-008) specific about which output streams are compared? [Clarity, Spec §SC-008]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Do the spec ("system log lines keep their default level") and the plan ("`system_log_level = "INFO"`") agree, and does either say why `REPORT` lines must stay? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. The two agree only through Lambda's default, which neither document states, and the reason for keeping REPORT lines is thin. Fix: as CHK001, plus one clause on why REPORT lines stay.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: FR-001 states INFO is Lambda's default, set explicitly, and why `REPORT` lines stay; it agrees with plan and R1.
- [x] CHK011 Are the forbidden extra-field names identical in FR-009, data-model.md (LogCall) and research R5? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK012 Are the stable keys the same in the spec's Key Entities, contracts/log-line.md and the staging query in quickstart.md? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. The staging query selects `@timestamp` (CloudWatch's time), not the line's `timestamp` key, so the check never sees a stable key. Fix: add `timestamp` to the query's fields.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: The quickstart query selects `timestamp` and the old keys `time` and `aws_request_id`.
- [x] CHK013 Is FR-019 ("the only infrastructure change is the logging configuration") consistent with the claim in the spec's Assumptions and the constitution check that `infra/monitoring.tf` is untouched? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK014 Can SC-006 be judged pass or fail from the query's output alone, with an explicit pass condition for each key? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. Check 4 ('no `time` or `aws_request_id`') cannot be judged because the query does not select them; zero rows is not called a fail; MKX is hard-coded though staging's offices are in gitignored tfvars. Fix: select those fields, say zero rows fails, say 'each staging office'.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: SC-006 and quickstart list five numbered pass conditions; zero rows fails; offices come from staging's configuration, not MKX.
- [x] CHK015 Is SC-005 ("logging code shrinks") stated as checkable absences, such as no formatter class and no request-id stamp, rather than as a size? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK016 Does an acceptance criterion require proof that the two message-based metric filters still count after the format change, and say where that proof comes from (staging, not offline)? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §US2, Spec §SC-003]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. SC-006 proves only the posts filter; the ambiguous filter is never exercised on staging, yet US2.4 says both filters still count. Fix: accept the ambiguous filter by inference (same key and text) or check it with `aws logs test-metric-filter`.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: US2 scenario 4, SC-006 and quickstart accept the ambiguous filter by inference from the posts filter (same key, same match form).

## Scenario and Recovery Coverage

- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for what happens when the staging check fails? Production approval is declined, but staging keeps the new format: is reverting it in scope? [Gap, Recovery]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. The only recovery step is declining production; staging keeps the new format and no document says whether or how to revert. Fix: FR-020 and quickstart say a failed check means a revert pull request.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: FR-020, research R10 and quickstart: decline production, then a revert pull request of the U2 merge puts staging back.
- [x] CHK018 Is the window between the staging and production deploys addressed, when the two environments write different line shapes? An example is a cross-environment query or the dashboard during that window. [Coverage, Gap]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. No document mentions the window between deploys, though the ground truth shows it is harmless (only `$.message` filters read the lines). Fix: one sentence in the spec's Assumptions.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: Spec Assumptions: the window is harmless, since only `$.message` filters read lines and the dashboard charts alarm metrics.
- [x] CHK019 Are the runtime's own lines (`START`, `END`, `REPORT`, its unhandled-error report) covered by a requirement on how U4 and U5 should treat them, or only by an edge-case note? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. U5 counts by `level`, and the runtime's unhandled-error report likely arrives at ERROR with no `event` on every failed run; no rule says to exclude it. Fix: contract filter guidance excludes event-less non-library lines and counts failed runs only from `Errors`.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: Spec Key Entities and the contract's filter guidance: count only lines with an `event` or a library logger; the runtime's error report is never counted.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK020 Is the effect of JSON lines on CloudWatch log volume and cost addressed, given constitution Principle VI's budget limit? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [x] CHK021 Does the spec say whether log retention and the log group are unchanged by the format switch? [Gap]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK022 Is the assumption that the runtime writes an attribute set by a record factory (`office`) as it writes `extra` keys stated in the spec itself, so that the staging check knows to test it? It appears only in research R4. [Assumption, Spec §FR-003]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. Spec Assumptions cover only `extra` fields; the record-factory claim appears only in research R4. Fix: state it in the spec and tie it to SC-006.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: Spec Assumptions state the record-factory assumption and tie it to SC-006 check 3.
- [x] CHK023 Is the accepted risk documented for a record the runtime cannot serialise, including whether such a record could be dropped from the alarm counts? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. The risk is accepted without saying an unserialisable record could be dropped from counts; every extra is JSON-native today, but no document says so. Fix: one sentence in the spec's Assumptions.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: Spec Assumptions accept the risk, say a broken line would drop from counts, and note every extra is JSON-native today.
- [x] CHK024 Is the assumption that the runtime's handler is in place before the package is imported, which covers library warnings at import time, recorded as an accepted, unverified assumption? [Assumption, Spec §Edge Cases]
  - Review 2026-11-09: not satisfied. The spec states as fact that the runtime handler exists before import; nothing marks it accepted and unverified. Fix: one sentence in the spec's Assumptions.
  - Fixed 2026-11-10: Spec Assumptions and Edge Cases mark the import-time handler as accepted and unverified.
